name: Foldkit
shortDescription: TypeScript front-end framework built on Effect and structured like Elm: one state value, one update function, side effects as data.
description: Foldkit is a TypeScript front-end framework built on Effect that follows The Elm Architecture. The whole state of an app is one value, the Model. Everything that happens is a Message, and one pure function, update, turns the current Model and a Message into the next Model plus any side effects to run, which are returned as values and not performed in place.

We are evaluating Foldkit, not adopting it. We built OK Tuner, a free browser instrument tuner, in Foldkit to find out how its architecture suits work where an AI coding agent writes most of the code and a person reviews it. What helped: state changes that are tested without a browser, state unions the compiler checks at every use, resources such as a microphone whose lifetime follows the Model, and a conventions file and DevTools server made for agents.

What it cost: more code than the Svelte component the tuner was ported from, views written as function calls and not markup, a large script for a small app, and two things to learn, of which Effect is the bigger. Foldkit is pre-1.0 and marks its server rendering experimental. SvelteKit remains our default for content sites and for anything that leans on a server.
